summary.headline: TII standalone Q4 FY26 revenue rose 16% YoY to Rs 2,279 Cr and PBT (pre-exceptional) rose 10% to Rs 361 Cr.
summary.overview: Standalone revenue for Q4 FY26 was Rs 2,279 Cr versus Rs 1,957 Cr a year earlier, with full-year revenue of Rs 8,556 Cr against Rs 7,893 Cr. Pre-exceptional PBT for the quarter was Rs 361 Cr versus Rs 327 Cr, and full-year ROIC held at 44%. Consolidated revenue rose to Rs 6,215 Cr from Rs 5,150 Cr, helped by CG Power (56% stake) revenue of Rs 3,442 Cr. Management described volumes as still strong, while flagging commodity and fuel cost inflation, partly recoverable from customers with a one-to-two-quarter lag. Growth in EV three-wheelers was held back in Q4 by a body-in-white supplier problem, now being resolved in-house.

guidance_outlook: Core standalone capex planned at Rs 300-350 Cr for FY27.
Around Rs 300 Cr rough estimate to go into subsidiaries in FY27 (TI Clean Mobility and TI Medical).
CDMO plant at Naidupet in final commissioning; commercial production to start next quarter (Q1 FY27).
TI Medical targeted to grow about 20% YoY; wound care (sutures) guided at 15-20% growth.
Three-wheeler production expected to return to normal capacity by end of Q1 FY27 after body-in-white supplier issue.
CRSS plant in Nasik expected to be 100% utilised by end FY26 or mid FY27; Western tube facilities at about 30% utilisation, targeted at 100% by mid FY27.
capex_capacity: Core capex FY27 guided at Rs 300-350 Cr.
Naidupet CDMO facility in final commissioning; commercial production expected from next quarter.
Acquired Medicura's Ambala IV cannula asset through an asset purchase; plant approvals and hiring underway, commercial production expected in Q1-Q2 FY27.
Three-wheeler body-in-white facility taken over from the supplier, near the existing unit; ramp-up reached targeted levels in April and May, with some teething issues remaining.
Hyundai's Western India plant started last quarter; supplied from TI's Pune facility, which is ramping up.
Railway product development complete; awaiting Government of India approval for Vande Bharat coach supply, expected to show progress in two to three quarters.
demand_pricing: Engineering volume growth broadly in line with sales growth in Q4, as there were no major price movements.

Management said volume growth remains strong going into Q1 FY27, though commodity and fuel inflation is a challenge; cost increases are recoverable from customers under contracts with a one-to-two-quarter lag.

EV trucks: TI holds about 28% share in the M&HCV segment (11 players) and about 27% in small commercial vehicles in Q4 (7 players); order book described as good, with deployments expected in Q1 and Q2.
EV deployment is constrained by financing (about Rs 100 Cr per 50-100 truck deployment, borne by the service provider) and charging infrastructure on routes.
Medical exports to the Middle East were hit by the war; Europe and Southeast Asia are growing.
Sodium-ion batteries are not expected to reduce TCO immediately, given long cell validation and vehicle integration timelines.

qa_highlights.question: What is the underlying volume growth in engineering?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume growth is in line with sales growth in Q4, as there were no major price movements.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand and cost pressure looking into Q1 FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is still strong; commodity and fuel inflation is the immediate challenge, with recovery from customers lagging by one to two quarters and internal cost reduction being pursued.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the railway business scale-up?
qa_highlights.answer: Product development is complete; approval from the Government of India for Vande Bharat coaches is pending, with progress expected in two to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: What are the EV volumes and the body-in-white issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 volumes were 87 M&HCVs, 241 small commercial vehicles and 1,176 three-wheelers. TI took over the body-in-white supplier's facility; management expects full normal supply by end of Q1 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CDMO timeline and FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: CDMO commercial production starts next quarter at Naidupet. Core capex is Rs 300-350 Cr, plus about Rs 300 Cr into subsidiaries (TICMPL and TI Medical).

qa_highlights.question: Why is MFP sluggish and what is the Medical outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: MFP slowness is attributed to railway tender profitability, new product development with private players, and Hyundai's muted growth; Hyundai's Western plant has started. TI Medical is targeted at about 20% growth after the Ambala asset purchase.

risks_watch: Commodity and fuel cost inflation, with recovery from customers lagged by one to two quarters.
EV deployment hampered by financing and charging infrastructure; delivery targets rest on Q1 and Q2 FY27.
Three-wheeler scale-up depends on the in-house body-in-white facility reaching normal capacity by end Q1 FY27.
Railway Vande Bharat approval timing is uncertain (two to three quarters).
Middle East disruption affecting medical exports; MFP weakness tied to Hyundai and railway tenders.
Competitive intensity in EV trucks (11 players) and small commercial vehicles (7 players).
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and capacity ramp-ups (CDMO, EV trucks, Western tube plants), but cautious on macro, fuel and commodity cost pressures. Several answers were hedged on timing, such as railway approvals and EV deployment, and no revenue figure was given for the Medicura acquisition.
